reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch trace the Chronicles date to a scribal mix-up of similar Hebrew numeral letters, turning an original sixteenth year into the thirty-sixth.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen presses that Chronicles' thirty-sixth-year date places Baasha's Judah campaign long after Kings already has him dead.

quotes.text: Baasha survived only to the twenty-sixth year of Asa, the wickedness must have been perpetrated before that date. … are brought down in Chronicles to the thirty-sixth year of the latter (xvi. 1). It has been properly observed that Baasha was at that date long dead,
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on 1 Kings 16:8 and 2 Chronicles 16:1.

sides.snippet: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel
sides.verseText: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, [and reigned] two years.

sides.snippet: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah
sides.verseText: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
